Subject: Dedicated deployment - region & data deletion Qs

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we proceed with procurement I need to confirm a few points for our privacy/security review around the planned Dedicated deployment:

- Can you confirm physical & logical isolation for a Dedicated pool pinned to the eu-west-1 region? Specifically: will any customer data or logs ever leave the EU boundary (including control-plane telemetry)?
- Backups & snapshots: are they stored in the same region by default, and what is the retention policy?
- Deletion/erasure: if we request data erasure, what is the end-to-end timeline for primary storage, backups, and any cached KV state? Do you provide evidence/artifacts once erasure completes?
- Can you provide a short attestation or runbook we can attach to our audit?

We're aiming to finalize security sign-off next week. Appreciate a concise reply and any attachments you can share.

Thanks,
Daniel Murray
Senior Cloud Security Manager
NovaBank

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, full notes below and two attachments (residency matrix + erasure runbook).

Summary answers:
- Region pinning & isolation: yes — Dedicated pools can be pinned to eu-west-1. Customer data at rest, runtime model inputs, and application-level logs for that pool remain in the pinned region. Control-plane metadata used for billing and orchestration is stored in Redwood control plane (US/EU split); we can configure the control-plane tenant for EU-only for Dedicated during provisioning.
- Backups/snapshots: by default backups for Dedicated are kept in the same region and encrypted with a customer-managed key (optional). Default snapshot retention is 30 days; we can reduce this or enable on-demand snapshot purge as part of SLA.
- Deletion/erasure timeline: standard process is: primary data erasure within 72 hours of request; backups and snapshots purged within 30 days unless you opt into an accelerated wipe (see runbook) which delivers verification within 72 hours for both primary and snapshots when backed by our wipe appliance and customer KMS keys.
- Evidence: we provide an erasure certificate (signed), a job-run log, and SHA256 manifests for wiped objects. We can place those artifacts into a shared Drive folder or via a signed S3 URL.

Details / caveats:
- Telemetry/control-plane: Redwood collects lightweight telemetry (health pings, scheduler events). For Dedicated EU tenants we can limit telemetry export to EU control-plane instances. If NovaBank requires zero-control-plane telemetry leaving EU, we offer a Private control-plane option (additional fee) or an on-prem control-plane.
- KV/cache: transient KV caches are scoped to the Dedicated pool and cleared on instance reclamation; the erasure job includes explicit cache invalidation and verification steps.
- Multi-tenant surface: Dedicated pool nodes are single-tenant at the container level; underlying host kernel is shared (as is typical in cloud VMs). If you need hypervisor-level tenancy we can discuss a single-tenant host option.

I've attached: "redwood-region-residency-matrix.csv" (region-by-region behavior) and "erasure-process.md" (step-by-step and artifacts). Karthik and Stephanie are on copy for technical follow-ups and to set a short walkthrough if helpful.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm whether NovaBank wants the EU control-plane or the Private control-plane option?
- Do you need faster backup purge SLA (24/72 hours) for an additional ops support contract?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Security
Redwood Inference

Hi team — adding the technical detail and a couple of artifacts to address LegalOps. Quick points:

- Attestation: we can provide a one-page attestation on Redwood letterhead confirming region residency behavior for Dedicated eu-west-1 pools (we'll draft and share a PDF).
- Artifacts: erasure certificate (PDF, signed), job-run log (JSON), file manifests (SHA256 list), and an optional Host-erase audit (CSV) for accelerated erasures. See attached "data-flow-diagram.svg" for how data flows into the Dedicated pool and "kms-integration-notes.pdf" for how keys are scoped.
- Telemetry: control-plane telemetry is strictly metadata (instance health, CPU, scheduling). No content blobs, prompts, or PII are included in those telemetry events. For customers with strict requirements we recommend the Private control-plane (we'll note this in the attestation).

Operational options we recommend:
- Default: EU control-plane + 30d snapshot retention + standard erasure (72h primary, 30d backup purge).
- Tight compliance: Private control-plane + 30d retention but accelerated wipe (72h for both primary & backups) + signed erasure artifacts (additional ops fee).

I've uploaded the diagram and KMS notes to the shared Drive link and attached them here for quick review. If you want, we can run a 45-min walkthrough next week to show the wipe job and certificate generation.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Inference Platforms
